newsitem.title: USA: Montana Power says settles with Puget.
newsitem.headline: Montana Power says settles with Puget.

text.p: Montana Power Co said Sunday it has settled all disputes with Puget Sound Light and Power Co over a power sales agreement and coal contracts.
As a result of the agreement, Montana Power said its annual revenues would drop by $11 million to $13 million.

The companies had been scheduled to go to trial Monday in U.S. District Court in Butte over a disputed power sales agreement for 94 megawatts of electricity from Colstrip Unit 4, which is owned by the two companies as well as Portland General Electric Co, Washington Water Power Co and PacifiCorp.
Puget had contended that a firm transmission path for the power it purchased had not been established, and that it had a right to terminate a 21-year purchase agreement scheduled to end in 2010.
Montana Power, the seller, contended that it had complied with the spirit and letter of the agreement since deliveries began October 1, 1989, and that Puget had no right to terminate the pact.

In addition to ending the power-sales dispute, the parties also resolved pending coal disputes between Puget and Montana Power's mining subsidiary, Western Energy, the owner and operator of the Rosebud Mine that supplies coal to the four mine-mouth generating plants operated by Montana Power.
"This settlement ends pending proceedings on a coal price reopener for Colstrip Units 1 & 2," Montana Power Chairman and Chief Executive Dan Berube said in a statement.
Puget also agreed to cease participation in a gross inequity claim against Western Energy by the four non-operating owners of Colstrip Units 3 & 4, Montana Power said.
In return, Montana Power agreed to cut the price for electricity sold to Puget under the power-sales agreement, and Western Energy agreed to reduce Puget's cost of coal, it said.
Montana Power said those agreements would reduce its revenues by between $11 million and $13 million, before anticipated efficiency gains that began January 1, 1997.

The agreements between the two companies calls for them to work together to obtain the commitment of all co-owners to restructure the existing contractual arrangements at the four Colstrip plants and the associated Rosebud Mine, it said.

"I am hopeful Montana Power, Western Energy and Puget can mediate all pending disputes with Colstrip's other non-operating owners this year," Montana Power Vice Chairman and President Bob Gannon said in a statement.
